title: Data Preparation to Perceptual Visualization
summary: Audit and standardize messy raw tables in DataMend Lab, then export a tidy CSV to discover perceptually honest encodings in VisualGrammar.
whyConnected: A chart is only as truthful as its underlying denominator and variable schema. Cleaning sentinel values (-999) and deduplicating primary keys prevents distorted visual distributions.

stages.action: Standardize mixed dates, recode sentinel strings to explicit NA, and reshape wide columns into a tidy observation-per-row table.
Load the exported tidy CSV into VisualGrammar, match variable types to Cleveland–McGill Rank 1–3 encodings, and verify Lie Factor = 1.00.

transferMethod: File-based handoff: Export validated UTF-8 CSV from DataMend Lab and import directly into VisualGrammar's Chart Studio (no external server upload).

title: Data Preparation to Computational Inference
summary: Verify unit-level independence and clean numeric measurements in DataMend Lab before running bootstrap confidence intervals or permutation tests in ResampleLab.
whyConnected: Bootstrap resampling and permutation tests assume each row represents a valid observational unit. Duplicate records or unstripped unit strings corrupt resampled standard errors.

stages.action: Confirm primary-key uniqueness, strip unit suffixes from numeric columns, and isolate missing values transparently.
Import the clean numeric/group columns into ResampleLab to run 10,000 bootstrap replicates or two-sample randomization tests.

transferMethod: File-based handoff: Export clean numeric/group CSV from DataMend Lab and load into ResampleLab.

title: Regression Diagnostics to Resampling Inference
summary: Inspect bivariate structure, leverage, and residual normality in QuartetLab, then move to ResampleLab when non-normal residuals or outliers call for bootstrap slope intervals.
whyConnected: Classical OLS t-intervals rely on normal, homoscedastic errors. When QuartetLab's Normal Q-Q or Cook's distance diagnostics reveal skewness or influential points, ResampleLab provides nonparametric bootstrap slope intervals.

stages.action: Examine scatter geometry, Residuals vs. Fitted, Normal Q-Q plots, and Cook's distance (D_i > 4/n).
Export bivariate pairs (x_i, y_i) from QuartetLab and construct bootstrap confidence intervals for β₁ or permutation null distributions for r.

transferMethod: File-based handoff: Export bivariate CSV from QuartetLab and import into ResampleLab's bivariate resampling mode.

title: Time-Series Preparation to Statistical Forecasting
summary: Regularize irregular timestamps, sort chronologically, and audit explicit calendar gaps in DataMend Lab before decomposing and forecasting in ForecastLab.
whyConnected: STL decomposition, ETS, and SARIMA models require a strictly ordered, regularly spaced temporal index (tsibble structure). Unsorted dates or implicit missing months invalidate lag operators and ACF calculations.

stages.action: Coerce mixed date formats to ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), deduplicate timestamps, and make implicit time gaps explicit.
Load the regularized series into ForecastLab to run STL decomposition, compare ETS/SARIMA against Seasonal Naïve via MASE, and project 80%/95% prediction intervals.

transferMethod: File-based handoff: Export chronologically sorted ISO-8601 CSV from DataMend Lab and load into ForecastLab.

title: Forecasting Output to Publication Graphics
summary: Generate calibrated point forecasts and 80%/95% prediction intervals in ForecastLab, then refine multi-series comparisons and perceptual color palettes in VisualGrammar.
whyConnected: Communicating forecasts to decision-makers requires distinguishing historical observations from projected horizons and encoding uncertainty bands with colorblind-safe OKLCH contrast.

stages.action: Fit and cross-validate time-series models, then export historical values alongside point predictions and 80%/95% lower/upper bounds.
Import the forecast table into VisualGrammar to apply OKLCH palettes, direct terminal labels, and pass the 15-point pre-flight audit.

transferMethod: File-based handoff: Export forecast CSV or SVG from ForecastLab and open in VisualGrammar.
